attempts.entry_title: Thalamic, mPFC and CA1 activity in non-REM sleep events (Varela and Wilson 2020)
attempts.summary: Most main findings held only in part here, and the maze findings could not be tested. SWR locking to mPFC delta and spindle phase reproduced, and SWR rate rose around K-complexes, but the thalamic rebound after them was only partly seen. Thalamic firing did not fall at SWRs or track SWR rate (1 of 3 units against 61.7%), and units were not less rhythmic than multi-unit activity. These results rest on 3 of the paper's 32 sessions and 5 thalamic units. Every comparison of sleep before and after the maze is untestable because the dataset holds no maze or pre-maze sleep.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Varela and Wilson (2020) on CRCNS hc-24, which holds three of the paper's sessions from three rats (units, tetrode multi-unit activity and LFP from midline thalamus, mPFC and CA1, with derived sleep periods, K-complexes, spindle troughs and SWRs). It tests the timing and phase of SWRs around mPFC K-complexes and spindles, the firing of units of the three regions around these events, and, in the session of sleep after maze exploration, how CA1 units labelled as active on the maze take part in spindle cycles and SWRs. The sleep before the maze, the maze epoch, position data and most of the paper's units are not in the data set.

outcomes.statement: Spindle cycles detected in sleep carry spectral power concentrated near 10 to 15 Hz in the mPFC and CA1 LFP, unlike cycles detected by the same algorithm in quiet or active waking, which have theta-like profiles.
outcomes.source: Figure 1, figure supplement 3 legend
outcomes.quote: Spindle cycles detected during sleep are associated with spectral power concentrated in the 10–15 Hz band, suggestive of spindle (and not theta) detection
outcomes.notes: No scaling of the scalogram meets both parts of the criterion. Relative to the state's mean power, the trough-triggered mPFC scalogram in sleep peaks at 11 Hz (S1) and 10 Hz (S3) under every trough reading, within 10 to 15 Hz, but CA1 troughs detected outside sleep peak at 13 Hz in S1 (sleep 11 to 12 Hz) and 9 to 10 Hz in S3 (sleep 9 Hz), so the waking CA1 peak is not lower. In raw power the S3 waking CA1 peak is lower (7 against 8 Hz) but the S3 mPFC sleep peak is at 4 to 8 Hz. Outside sleep is all time outside the deposited sleep periods in the box (97 to 488 troughs), which includes any REM sleep; no active waking on the maze is in the data set. Up to 800 troughs per condition (seeded subset). Question for the authors, recorded as a finding: how the scalogram of Figure 1, figure supplement 3 was normalised.
deviations: Wavelet power shown both raw and relative to the mean power of the same LFP in the same state at each frequency; the paper does not say how the scalogram is scaled. The outcome is the same under both.

findings.statement: The data set holds 3 recording sessions (about 3.5 h, 5 thalamic units) of the paper's 32 sessions with thalamic units (63 thalamic units). It holds no maze epoch, no sleep before the maze, none of the four long control sessions and no position (LED) data, so the paper's comparisons of sleep before and after the maze (six claims) and the waking definition by velocity cannot be tested, and most unit-level claims rest on 2 to 13 units.

The thalamic nucleus of each unit is not given; only the Session 1 unit is named (MD), in the title of a deposited script. Session 2's two units sit in a folder with no region in its name and are thalamic only by the deposited script's title. The LFP files state no unit, and the descriptor does not say which tetrode and wire each LFP comes from.

The deposited spindle troughs do not follow the detection rule of the Methods (local minima three sd below the mean of the spindle-filtered LFP): they are 3.7 to 6.2 times as many as that rule gives (3817 against 1019 in Session 1) and their filtered values reach -0.7 to -1.1 sd. The deposited Session 1 SWRs (1263) are also more than the Methods' k = 3 rule gives (840). Question for the authors: what threshold and reference period produced the deposited troughs and SWRs, and were these the events behind the paper's figures?

Question for the authors: how was the spindle-trough-triggered scalogram of Figure 1, figure supplement 3 scaled (raw wavelet power, or power relative to a baseline)? This attempt shows both raw power and power relative to the mean power of the same state; in raw power the Session 3 mPFC peak falls at 4 to 8 Hz, not 10 to 15 Hz.

Spike times are stored at single precision. In Session 3 every spike time equals its float32 rounding, a resolution of 2^-10 s (0.98 ms) at these values, which produces repeated timestamps (6230 in the thalamic MUA, 657 in the mPFC MUA, 17 and 8 in two thalamic units); in Sessions 1 and 2, 73 to 87 % of times do. LFP and event times are in double precision.

In Session 3 the mPFC unit and MUA start at 11750 s, 24 min before the LFP, the sleep periods and every other stream (13200 s); the descriptor does not say what this epoch is. The CA1 files labelled "InRun" hold only spikes of the sleep after the maze; the maze spikes behind the label are not included.

The paper's Data availability statement names the CRCNS data set "HC-24" (doi:10.6080/K0K35RVG) and then says that the data set and the documentation that describes it are available as "HC-19" (crcns.org/data-sets/hc/hc-19). The hc-24 data descriptor (version 0.6) cites the 2019 bioRxiv preprint (doi:10.1101/653436), not the eLife paper.

The Methods' sleep rule, mPFC delta power and CA1 ripple power both above the session mean for at least 2 min, finds no sleep in Sessions 1 and 3 when power is a 1 s or 10 s moving average of the squared filtered LFP, against 42 and 78 min of deposited sleep. Filling dips shorter than 30 s finds 19 and 44 min inside the deposited periods. Question for the authors: what smoothing, and what tolerance for short dips, produced the deposited sleep periods?

entries.name: varela-2020
entries.title: Thalamic, mPFC and CA1 activity in non-REM sleep events (Varela and Wilson 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Varela and Wilson (2020) on CRCNS hc-24, which holds three of the paper's sessions from three rats (units, tetrode multi-unit activity and LFP from midline thalamus, mPFC and CA1, with derived sleep periods, K-complexes, spindle troughs and SWRs). It tests the timing and phase of SWRs around mPFC K-complexes and spindles, the firing of units of the three regions around these events, and, in the session of sleep after maze exploration, how CA1 units labelled as active on the maze take part in spindle cycles and SWRs. The sleep before the maze, the maze epoch, position data and most of the paper's units are not in the data set.
